## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Asampadānajātaka* (Ja 131) is a story in the Pali Jātaka collection belonging to the first book (*Ekanipāta*) [Fausböll 1877]. The narrative was delivered by the Buddha while residing at the Bamboo Grove (Veḷuvana) near Rājagaha, occasioned by a discussion among the monks in the Dhamma hall regarding the ungrateful nature of Devadatta and his failure to acknowledge the Buddha's kindness [Fausböll 1877]. In response, the Buddha explains that Devadatta's ingratitude was not confined to his present life but was demonstrated in bygone times as well.

In the story of the past, the Bodhisatta was born as the merchant Saṅkha-seṭṭhi, while Devadatta was the merchant Piliya-seṭṭhi [Fausböll 1877]. When Piliya fell on hard times, the Bodhisatta generously gave him half of his own fortune; however, when the Bodhisatta himself later came to be in need, Piliya ungratefully offered him merely rice gruel [Anandajoti 2010]. The Bodhisatta nevertheless accepted the offering in order to honor and preserve the obligations of friendship [Anandajoti 2010]. The canonical verse opening begins with the words *Asampadānena itarītarassa* [Fausböll 1877].
